original_question: Determine whether there exists a II1 factor N with no diffuse relative-(T) subalgebras and with a unique sequential commutation orbit, and whether such an N can additionally have the Haagerup property.
target_in_paper: Section "Sequential commutation", Problem 24 of arXiv:2511.20377. This paper is a list of open problems, so the relevant target is Problem 24 rather than any Conjecture 1.1/Proposition 1.2/Theorem 1.3.
correct_elements: Your draft already captures the right official target almost verbatim: it asks for a II_1 factor N, requires that N have no diffuse relative-(T) subalgebras, asks that N have a unique sequential commutation orbit, and then asks for the strengthened variant in which N also has the Haagerup property.
missing_details: The paper’s sequential commutation relation is on Haar unitaries, not on arbitrary elements or arbitrary unitaries.
To make the question stand-alone, one should define a Haar unitary u in a tracial von Neumann algebra (N, tau) by tau(u^m)=0 for every integer m>=1.
One should spell out that the sequential commutation relation is defined using a fixed nonprincipal ultrafilter U on N and the tracial ultrapower N^U.

A self-contained version should unpack "unique sequential commutation orbit" as: any two Haar unitaries u,v in N are equivalent, meaning there is a finite path of Haar unitaries in N^U from u to v with consecutive terms commuting.
The phrase "no diffuse relative-(T) subalgebras" should be made explicit as: there is no diffuse von Neumann subalgebra A⊂N such that the inclusion A⊂N has Popa’s relative property (T).
The paper asks two existential questions: first, whether such an N exists at all; second, whether one can choose such an N to have the Haagerup property as an additional hypothesis.
No extra assumptions such as separability, Connes embeddability, property Gamma/non-Gamma, solidity, or strong solidity are part of Problem 24, so these should not be added.
refined_question: Fix a nonprincipal ultrafilter U on N. Does there exist a II_1 factor N with faithful normal trace tau such that N has no diffuse von Neumann subalgebra A⊂N for which the inclusion A⊂N has Popa’s relative property (T), and such that the sequential commutation equivalence relation on the Haar unitaries of N has a single orbit; equivalently, for every pair of Haar unitaries u,v in N (that is, tau(u^m)=tau(v^m)=0 for all m>=1), there exist Haar unitaries w_1,...,w_n in N^U with [u,w_1]=0, [w_k,w_{k+1}]=0 for 1<=k<n, and [w_n,v]=0? Can one moreover choose N to have the Haagerup property?
justification: The draft is targeting the paper’s official Problem 24 in the section "Sequential commutation." The nearby introductory paragraph to that section supplies the hidden notation needed to make the question self-contained: the sequential commutation relation is an equivalence relation on Haar unitaries, defined through finite commuting paths in an ultrapower, and the paper’s global conventions specify the use of a fixed nonprincipal ultrafilter and tracial ultrapowers. I therefore kept the scope exactly at Problem 24, only unpacking the definitions needed to make the question stand alone, and I did not add any hypotheses not present in the paper.
